title: Reduce hot-tenant index churn with heatmap and tunable compaction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce query latency and write amplification caused by frequently added/removed indexes and wide control_plane rows. This ticket introduces an index usage heatmap pipeline and an adaptive index sweeper that can suggest and optionally remove low-value indexes, plus a selective column compaction path for large JSONB payloads to reduce row width and improve index maintenance costs.
background: Over the past year we've repeatedly seen spikes in DDL churn on tenant-scoped tables as teams add narrow indexes for short-lived analytical queries. These indexes increase WAL, slow DML for hot tenants, and cause long index bloat cycles. Additionally, control_plane.rows contain several large JSONB blobs that are hot-for-write but cold-for-read; they increase IO and index maintenance costs. Previous efforts (ENG-24601, ENG-28901, ENG-41205) reduced some hotspots but did not provide ongoing detection or safe automated cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap pipeline runs hourly and stores index usage metrics per-tenant for the last 90 days
Adaptive sweeper can generate a ranked list of candidate indexes for removal with estimated cost delta and safety checks
Selective compaction path moves <<large_jsonb_fields>> to a side table with online backfill and application-transparent joins
No customer-facing queries regress >5% p95 latency after rollout (measured on synthetic workload and canary tenants)
All DDL performed online with locks limited to metadata levels and automated rollback path verified
migration_steps: Deploy heatmap collector: lightweight pg_stat_statements + periodic sample of pg_index and pg_stat_all_indexes matched to tenant_id
Run a 14-day observation window on staging to calibrate heat thresholds and false-positive rate
Create compaction side-table schema for large_json_payloads and deploy application feature-flag that reads from both places
Backfill side-table using batched, rate-limited UPDATE -> INSERT pattern with statement_timeout and retry logic
Introduce adaptive-sweeper as a dry-run job: generate candidate lists, annotate with estimated WAL and CPU impact, open review tickets for each tenant group
After review window, enable opt-in removal flag for non-critical tenants; monitor queries and error rates for 48h before wider rollout
rollback_steps: If read latency regressions observed: disable sweeper, re-create dropped indexes from stored CREATE INDEX statements snapshot
If backfill causes WAL pressure: pause backfill, resume with smaller batches and lower concurrent workers
If data divergence observed between main row and side-table: stop feature-flag and run reconciliation job using stored operation log
monitoring_queries: Dashboard: index_churn_rate = count(index_create_drop_events) / day by tenant
WAL_increase_by_tenant = sum(wal_bytes) grouped by tenant over 1h
p95_query_latency_controlplane = percentile_cont(0.95) of duration for control_plane.* routes by tenant
index_usage_heatmap = top N indexes by num_scans and last_scan_age (from pg_stat_all_indexes)
index_bloat_alert = pgstattuple estimate > 40% or index_size_growth_rate > 2x week-over-week
